# chainguard_auth_policy (Resource)

The authentication policy of a root, verified organization: how long a sign-in to the organization lasts before its members must sign in again.

Every such organization has exactly one policy, so this resource never creates or deletes one. Creating the resource sets the session length; destroying it returns the organization to Chainguard's default length.

The length runs from login. At 30 days or less, a session lasts that long from login, and using it does not extend it. Above 30 days, a session lasts while it is used at least once every 30 days, up to the length. A session whose client does not rotate its refresh tokens lasts at most 20 hours; chainctl rotates them.

A member of several organizations gets the shortest length among them.

A shorter length reaches an existing session at its next token refresh only when a length over 20 hours has already extended that session past 20 hours from login. It does not cut any other existing session: that session keeps the expiry it was issued with, at most 20 hours from login.

The policy's sso_only control is not managed by this resource. SSO-only enforcement has not shipped yet.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Sessions last up to 30 days from login. At 30 days or less, use does not
# extend a session.
resource "chainguard_auth_policy" "example" {
  parent_id        = "fb694596eb1678321f94eec283e1e0be690f655c"
  session_duration = "720h"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `parent_id` (String) The UIDP of the root, verified organization this policy belongs to.
- `session_duration` (String) How long a sign-in to the organization lasts, from 1h to 90d, in whole seconds. Either a Go duration such as `720h` or a whole number of days such as `30d`. A value read back from the API is written in hours (`720h`), or in minutes or seconds when it is not a whole number of hours; a configured value that names the same length, such as `30d` for `720h`, is kept as written.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The UIDP of the organization, the same as parent_id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An auth policy can be imported by specifying the UIDP of its root organization
terraform import chainguard_auth_policy.example fb694596eb1678321f94eec283e1e0be690f655c
```
